s: The seeds fall on four kinds of ground, with different outcomes: eaten, withered, choked, or fruitful. Jesus explains that they represent the word of the Kingdom sown in the hearts of those who hear.

l: parables (Jesus's teaching method), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: Jesus speaks to the multitudes only in parables, and explains to the disciples that this is because the crowds see and hear without understanding, fulfilling Isaiah's prophecy. The chapter also presents it as fulfilling the saying 'I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the foundation of the world.'

l: man with the wheat field (parable of the darnel), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: The man sows good seed in his field, and an enemy sows darnel among the wheat while people sleep. He tells his servants not to uproot the darnel, so the wheat is not harmed, and says he will have the reapers gather the darnel to burn and the wheat into his barn at harvest.

l: parable of the darnel weeds, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A parable in Chapter 13: an enemy sows darnel among wheat and both grow together until harvest; Jesus then explains the sower as the Son of Man, field as the world, darnel as the evil one's children, enemy as the devil.

l: harvest (end of the age), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: Jesus explains that the harvest is the end of the age and the reapers are angels. The angels will gather out of the Kingdom all that causes stumbling and those who do iniquity and cast them into the furnace of fire, while the righteous will shine like the sun in their Father's Kingdom.

l: Jesus's home country, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: Jesus comes into his own country and teaches in the synagogue there. He does not do many mighty works there because of the people's unbelief.

l: people of Jesus's country, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: Jesus's hometown people are astonished by his wisdom and works but doubt him, citing his carpenter father and familiar family. They take offense, and their unbelief limits his mighty works there.

l: Herod the tetrarch, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: Herod, a tetrarch also called king, brother of Philip, imprisoned John the Baptizer for Herodias's sake, feared the multitude, then grievously beheaded him because of a birthday oath; hearing of Jesus, he believes John has risen from the dead.

l: Herodias, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: is_wife_of Philip [Philip is Herod's brother] Herodias is the wife of Herod's brother Philip, and John was imprisoned for her sake. She prompts her daughter to ask for John's head on a platter, and the head is brought to her.

l: daughter of Herodias, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: has_mother Herodias Herodias's daughter dances at Herod's birthday and pleases him, so he promises with an oath to give her whatever she asks. Prompted by her mother, she asks for John's head on a platter, receives it, and brings it to her mother.

l: multitudes (crowds following Jesus), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: The crowds follow Jesus on foot from the cities when he withdraws, and he heals their sick. They sit on the grass and all eat and are filled from the five loaves and two fish, numbering about five thousand men besides women and children. Jesus then sends them away.

l: beheading of John, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: Herod, grieved but bound by his oaths and the guests at his table, commands that John's head be given to Herodias's daughter, and John is beheaded in the prison. His head is brought on a platter to the young lady and then to her mother, and John's disciples bury the body and tell Jesus.

l: five loaves for the five thousand, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A miraculous feeding: at evening Jesus seats the crowds, blesses and breaks five loaves and two fish, disciples distribute them, about five thousand men plus women and children all eat and are filled, and twelve baskets of pieces remain.

l: boat (disciples' boat), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: Jesus withdraws by boat to a deserted place, and later makes the disciples board a boat to go ahead of him. In the middle of the sea it is distressed by waves and contrary wind; Peter steps out of it, and when Jesus and Peter get into it the wind ceases and those in it worship him.

l: sea, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: The disciples' boat is in the middle of the sea, distressed by waves and a contrary wind, when Jesus comes to them in the fourth watch. Jesus and Peter walk on its waters, and the wind ceases once they are in the boat; afterward they cross over to Gennesaret.

l: Jesus walking on the sea, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: occurs_during fourth watch of the night In the fourth watch of the night Jesus comes to the disciples walking on the sea, and they cry out in fear thinking he is a ghost. He tells them to cheer up and not be afraid, invites Peter to come, and rescues him when he sinks; the wind ceases and the disciples worship him as the Son of God.

l: Canaanite woman, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A Canaanite woman from the borders of Tyre and Sidon begs Jesus to have mercy on her demon-possessed daughter. Despite silence, rebuff, and a remark about dogs, she persists in worship and humble reply. Jesus praises her great faith, and her daughter is healed.

l: tradition of the elders, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: The tradition of the elders, which includes washing hands before eating bread, is the basis of the Pharisees' charge against the disciples. Jesus says it leads people to disobey and void God's commandment, and quotes Isaiah that teaching men's rules as doctrine makes worship vain.

l: commandment of God, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: commands honor of father and mother The commandment of God to honor father and mother, with death for whoever speaks evil of them, is cited by Jesus against the Pharisees. He says they make it void through their tradition, allowing a person to declare help owed to parents a gift devoted to God.

l: defilement, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: Defilement, as taught by Jesus in Chapter 15, comes not from food or eating with unwashed hands, which pass through the belly, but from the heart: what proceeds from the mouth, including evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, sexual sins, thefts, false testimony, and blasphemies.

l: scribes and the Pharisees, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: The scribes and Pharisees are a group of religious leaders who sit on Moses' seat of authority yet fail to practice what they teach, binding heavy burdens on others and acting to be seen by men and win honor and titles. Jesus pronounces repeated woes on them as hypocrites: they shut the Kingdom of Heaven against men, make proselytes twice as much sons of Gehenna, and neglect justice, mercy, and faith. Likened to whitened tombs, outwardly beautiful but inwardly unclean, they are called children of the prophets' killers and offspring of vipers, facing judgment upon this generation.

l: multitude, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: glorifies God [the God of Israel, after seeing healings] Jesus summons the multitude and tells them to hear and understand that what comes out of the mouth defiles. Great multitudes bring the lame, blind, mute, maimed, and others to him, wonder at the healings, and glorify the God of Israel. Having stayed with him three days with nothing to eat, they sit, eat, and are filled, and are then sent away.

l: seven loaves for the four thousand, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: Out of compassion for the multitude, Jesus takes seven loaves and a few small fish, gives thanks, breaks them, and has disciples distribute them. All eat and are filled; seven baskets of pieces remain, with four thousand men fed besides women and children.

l: Sadducees, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: The Sadducees are a group who deny the resurrection. They first join the Pharisees to test Jesus with a demand for a sign, earning rebuke and a warning about their teaching as yeast; later their seven-brothers question is answered by Jesus, silencing them.

l: yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: is_a teaching [of the Pharisees and Sadducees] Jesus told his disciples to beware of this yeast, which they first took to be about bread. After Jesus explained, they understood it meant the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

l: Elijah, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: Elijah appears on the mountain talking with Jesus, with Peter proposing a tent for him. Jesus says Elijah comes first to restore all things, has already come unrecognized, which disciples understand as John the Baptizer.

l: Christ, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: The Christ is a title-bearing figure whose identity is the central question. Peter declares Jesus the Christ, Son of the living God, revealed by the Father, and disciples are told to keep it secret. Later, the Pharisees call the Christ David's son, and Jesus questions that.

l: assembly (Jesus's assembly), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: Jesus said he will build his assembly on the rock, identified with Peter, and that the gates of Hades will not prevail against it. Peter is promised the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven, with binding and releasing on earth having been bound and released in heaven.

l: Jesus's suffering, death, and resurrection, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: Jesus foretells that he must go to Jerusalem, suffer much at the hands of elders, chief priests, and scribes, be killed, and be raised on the third day; Peter objects and is rebuked.

l: cost of discipleship, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: requires self-denial [also taking up one's cross and following Jesus] Jesus taught that anyone who desires to come after him must deny himself, take up his cross, and follow him. He said whoever tries to save his life will lose it, whoever loses it for his sake will find it, and nothing gained in the world is worth forfeiting one's life.

l: voice (from the cloud), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A voice comes out of a bright cloud that overshadows the mountain. It declares Jesus to be the beloved Son in whom it is well pleased and tells the hearers to listen to him.

l: man (father of the epileptic boy), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: The man kneels before Jesus and asks mercy for his epileptic son, who often falls into fire and water. He explains that he had brought the boy to the disciples, who could not cure him.

l: boy (the man's son), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: An epileptic boy, son of a man, suffers grievously, often falling into fire and water; Jesus rebukes the demon in Chapter 17, it leaves, and he is cured from that hour.

l: demon (possessing the boy), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: possesses boy (the man's son) [cast out by Jesus] The demon afflicts the boy. Jesus rebukes it, and it goes out of him. Jesus says this kind goes out only by prayer and fasting.

l: faith (as a grain of mustard seed), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: enables moving a mountain [nothing impossible for those with it] Jesus tells the disciples their failure to cast out the demon was due to unbelief. He says that faith as small as a mustard seed could make a mountain move from here to there, and that nothing would be impossible for them.

l: didrachma collectors, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: collect didrachma [at Capernaum] The collectors of the didrachma coins come to Peter in Capernaum and ask whether his teacher pays the didrachma. Peter answers yes, and they are later to receive payment from the stater coin Jesus provides.

l: didrachma, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: The didrachma is the coin collected in Capernaum, and the collectors ask whether Jesus pays it. Jesus argues that the children of kings are exempt, but says they will pay anyway so as not to cause stumbling.

l: stater coin, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: is_found_in fish (first caught) [in its mouth; to pay for Jesus and Peter] Jesus says Peter will find a stater in the mouth of the first fish he catches with a hook in the sea. Peter is to give it to the collectors for Jesus and himself.

l: Jesus's death and resurrection, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A prophesied event in which Jesus, as the Son of Man, foretells his own fate. In Chapter 17 he tells the disciples he will suffer at men's hands, be killed, and be raised on the third day, grieving them. In Chapter 20, going up to Jerusalem, he tells the twelve he will be delivered to chief priests and scribes, condemned, handed to Gentiles to be mocked, scourged and crucified, then raised on the third day.

l: disciples, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: asks Jesus [who is greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven] The disciples ask Jesus who is greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven. Jesus sets a child among them and tells them they must turn and become like little children to enter the Kingdom.

l: little child (set in the middle of the disciples), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: is_example_of humility [model for greatness in the Kingdom] Jesus calls the little child to himself and places the child in the middle of the disciples. The child serves as the example of humility: whoever humbles himself like this child is greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven, and whoever receives such a child in Jesus' name receives him.

l: little ones (who believe in Jesus), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: Believers in Jesus called little ones are valued and protected: Jesus warns that causing them to stumble deserves severe punishment, forbids despising them, notes their angels always see the Father's face, and affirms the Father does not will any to perish.

l: occasions of stumbling, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: is_inevitable must come [woe to the one through whom they come] Jesus says woe comes to the world because of them and to the person through whom they come, though they must come. He teaches that a hand, foot, or eye that causes stumbling should be cut off or plucked out, since entering life maimed or with one eye is better than being cast into the Gehenna of fire.

l: brother who sins, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: is_treated_as Gentile [if he refuses to hear the assembly] If he sins against someone, that person should show him his fault privately, then with one or two witnesses, then before the assembly. If he refuses to hear even the assembly, he is to be treated as a Gentile or a tax collector, but if he listens, the brother is regained.

l: church discipline (binding and releasing), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: has_effect bound or released in heaven [what is bound or released on earth] Jesus says that whatever is bound on earth will have been bound in heaven, and whatever is released on earth will have been released in heaven. He adds that agreement of two on earth in prayer will be done by the Father, and that where two or three gather in his name he is among them.

l: forgiveness, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: is_required_of disciples [from the heart, until seventy times seven] Jesus tells Peter to forgive not seven times but seventy times seven. The parable of the king and servants shows that having been forgiven a great debt calls for mercy to others, and that the heavenly Father will deal severely with those who do not forgive their brothers from the heart.

l: king (in the parable), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A king and lord of servants who settles accounts, compassionately forgives a servant's enormous debt, then, learning that servant was merciless to a fellow servant, angrily calls him wicked and delivers him to tormentors until he pays everything.

l: unforgiving servant, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A servant owing the king ten thousand talents is forgiven after begging patience, then jails a fellow servant owing one hundred denarii. The king calls him wicked and delivers him to tormentors until he pays everything due.

l: fellow servant (who owed one hundred denarii), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A servant owing one hundred denarii to the unforgiving servant; grabbed by the throat, he begs patience but is imprisoned until he pays, and fellow servants report it to the lord.

l: rich young man (the one who came to Jesus), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A wealthy young man who has kept the commandments since youth asks Jesus what good thing earns eternal life and what he still lacks. Told to sell his possessions, give to the poor, and follow Jesus, he leaves sad.

l: divorce, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: Divorce is a contested practice: Moses allowed it due to hardened hearts, though not intended from the beginning. Jesus permits it only for sexual immorality; otherwise divorcing and remarrying, or marrying a divorced woman, is adultery.

l: marriage, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: Marriage is described by Jesus as a man leaving his parents and joining his wife so the two become one flesh, joined by God and not to be separated. Disciples then call marrying inexpedient; Jesus says not all can accept this, mentioning eunuchs for the Kingdom.

l: eternal life, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: is_inherited_by those who leave family and lands for Jesus [also receive one hundred times] The young man asks what good thing he must do to have eternal life, and Jesus tells him to enter life by keeping the commandments, then to sell his goods, give to the poor, and follow him. At the end Jesus says everyone who leaves family or lands for his name's sake will receive a hundredfold and inherit eternal life.

l: possessions and wealth, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: hinders_entry_to Kingdom of Heaven [rich enter with difficulty] The young man's great possessions lead him to go away sad when Jesus tells him to sell them and give to the poor for treasure in heaven. Jesus says a rich man enters the Kingdom with difficulty, comparing it to a camel going through a needle's eye. He says those who leave houses, lands, and family for his name will receive a hundredfold.

l: master of the household (parable), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A household master in a parable who owns a vineyard and calls himself good. He hires laborers from early morning through the eleventh hour, then has his manager pay all a denarius, last to first, answering the complaining first-hired that he did no wrong.

l: laborers (parable), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: Parable group of vineyard laborers hired at different hours, all paid the same denarius regardless of hours worked; the first-hired murmur at equality with the last, and the master tells one to take his pay and go.

l: chief priests, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: The chief priests, acting with the scribes and elders, are a group consistently opposed to Jesus. In chapter 21 they are indignant at his wonders, question his authority, fail to answer his question about John's baptism, and want to seize him but fear the crowds. In chapter 26 they gather in Caiaphas's court, plan to arrest him by deceit apart from the feast, pay Judas thirty pieces of silver, send an armed crowd, and seek false testimony. In chapter 27 they take counsel to put him to death, deliver him to Pilate, buy the potter's field with the returned silver, persuade the crowd to ask for Barabbas, mock him on the cross, and have the tomb sealed with a guard. In chapter 28 they bribe the soldiers with silver to claim the disciples stole the body.

l: mother of the sons of Zebedee, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: is_mother_of sons of Zebedee She comes to Jesus with her sons, kneeling, and asks that they sit one on his right and one on his left in his Kingdom. Jesus replies that she does not know what she is asking.

l: sons of Zebedee, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A pair of brothers, two sons of Zebedee, approach Jesus with their mother; they affirm they can drink his cup and share his baptism. Jesus says they will, but the seats are the Father's to give, and the other ten grow indignant.

l: two blind men, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: Two blind men beside the road near Jericho cry out to Jesus as Lord and son of David despite the crowd's rebuke; he touches their eyes, they instantly see, and they follow him.

l: multitudes (crowds around Jesus), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A great multitude spreads clothes and branches, shouting 'Hosanna to the son of David!' and identifying Jesus as the Nazareth prophet. Holding John the Baptist likewise a prophet, they deter the fearful chief priests and Pharisees from seizing Jesus.

l: temple, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: The temple is called a house of prayer in Scripture, yet sellers and buyers made it a den of robbers. Jesus enters, drives out the traders, heals the lame and blind, receives children's Hosanna, and teaches there despite challenges from chief priests and elders. It sanctifies the gold within it. Later, shown its buildings, he foretells destruction, with not one stone left on another, and an abomination standing in the holy place.

l: fig tree, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A fig tree by the road bearing only leaves, no fruit; hungry Jesus curses it to never bear fruit, it withers immediately, and he uses the event to teach disciples about faith and prayer.

l: Jesus' authority, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: is_questioned_by chief priests [with the elders of the people] The chief priests and elders ask by what authority Jesus does these things and who gave it to him. Jesus answers with a question about whether John's baptism was from heaven or from men. Because they will not answer, he declines to tell them the source of his authority.

l: tax collectors and prostitutes, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A group of tax collectors and prostitutes who believed John the Baptist and, Jesus says, enter God's Kingdom ahead of the unrepentant chief priests and elders.

l: parable of the two sons, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: teaches first son did the father's will [the one who changed his mind and went] Jesus tells of a man whose first son says he will not work in the vineyard but afterward changes his mind and goes, while the second says 'I'm going, sir' but does not go. The leaders answer that the first did the father's will. Jesus applies it to them: the tax collectors and prostitutes who believed John are like the first son.

l: parable of the wicked farmers, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: features master of the household (vineyard owner) Jesus tells of a vineyard leased to farmers who beat, kill and stone the owner's servants and then kill his son. The leaders themselves say the owner will destroy those men and lease the vineyard to others. Jesus follows with the rejected stone saying, and the chief priests and Pharisees perceive that the parable is about them.

l: master of the household (vineyard owner), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A vineyard-owning master plants and equips a vineyard, leases it to farmers, and goes abroad. He sends servants, then his son, for the fruit. Leaders judge he will destroy the farmers and lease the vineyard to others who give fruit.

l: farmers (vineyard tenants), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: kills son (vineyard master's son) [to seize inheritance] The farmers beat one servant, kill another and stone another, and treat a second group of servants the same way. They kill the owner's son to seize his inheritance. The leaders judge that they will be miserably destroyed and replaced by other farmers.

l: son (vineyard master's son), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: is_a heir The master sends his son last, saying 'They will respect my son.' The farmers recognize him as the heir, throw him out of the vineyard and kill him. Jesus follows with the stone the builders rejected, which became the head of the corner.

l: temple cleansing, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: involves money changers' tables overthrown [Jesus drove out sellers and buyers] Jesus drives out all who sold and bought in the temple and overturns the money changers' tables and the dove sellers' seats. He cites 'My house shall be called a house of prayer' and accuses them of making it a den of robbers. Afterward he heals the lame and blind there, and the chief priests and scribes become indignant.

l: king (in the parable of the wedding feast), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: has_son son (the king's son) The king makes a wedding feast for his son and sends servants to call the invited, who refuse. He destroys the murderers and burns their city, has others invited from the highways, and orders the man without wedding clothing bound and thrown into the outer darkness.

l: servants (the king's servants), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: The servants are sent to call the invited guests, and some are seized, shamefully treated and killed. They are then sent to the highways and gather all they find, both bad and good, and later the king orders them to bind and remove the man without wedding clothing.

l: invited guests (of the wedding feast), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: has_state unworthy [as judged by the king] The invited guests refuse to come, make light of the invitation, and go to their farm or merchandise, while the rest kill the king's servants. The king declares them unworthy, destroys them and burns their city.

l: wedding feast (the king's son's), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: hosted_by king (in the parable of the wedding feast) The wedding feast is prepared with cattle and fatlings killed and everything ready. After the invited refuse, it is filled with guests gathered from the highways, both bad and good.

l: man without wedding clothing, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A guest lacking wedding clothing is noticed by the king, questioned about entering, left speechless, then ordered bound hand and foot and cast into outer darkness with weeping and grinding of teeth.

l: Caesar, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: owns denarius [image and inscription on it] Caesar's image and inscription are on the denarius shown to Jesus. Jesus says to give to Caesar the things that are Caesar's.
